citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen (2023). MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen (IN.AI Research, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, Carnegie Mellon University, University of Victoria, Princeton University)
description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering) across 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types. The ziyjiang/MMEB_Test_Instruct variant is a test/instruct split of MMMU used for multimodal embedding benchmarking.
name: MMMU (Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark)
publisher: ziyjiang (HuggingFace); original MMMU dataset from IN.AI Research / University of Waterloo / The Ohio State University
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students (including co-authors) from various disciplines and subjects, specializing in the majors covered by the benchmark. Affiliated with institutions including IN.AI Research, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, Carnegie Mellon University, University of Victoria, and Princeton University.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human expert performance was evaluated using 90 college senior students (3 per subject) on the 900 validation questions. Expert accuracy ranged from 76.2% (worst) to 88.6% (best), with a median of 82.6%, establishing a human performance baseline for the benchmark.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom web interface developed by Tianyu Zheng for data annotation and verification
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators (over 50 university students specializing in the relevant majors) collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources. All questions must contain one or more images, be written in English, meet college-level difficulty, and be unambiguous. Annotators categorized each question as multiple-choice or open-ended, and annotated fields including question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation (if available). Data was stored in JSON format. A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence, with regular audits of random samples.
rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. Subjects like law and linguistics were excluded because it was difficult to find enough relevant multimodal problems. Annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers to mitigate data contamination concerns.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected in three stages: (1) selection of 30 subjects from six disciplines based on the principle that visual inputs are commonly adopted; (2) recruitment of over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in these majors as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary; (3) quality control including deduplication, format/typo checking, and difficulty categorization. Annotators adhered to copyright and licensing regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copying or redistribution. Questions without immediately available answers were preferred to mitigate data contamination.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions collected from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and free online resources. The initial collection resulted in approximately 13K questions from various sources before quality filtering.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and "90th percentile of skilled adults," nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI as defined by Morris et al.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two-stage data cleaning: (1) lexical overlap and source URL similarity checks to identify potential duplicate problems, followed by author review to eliminate duplications; (2) distribution of problems among co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format. In a third stage, problems were categorized into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), and approximately 10% classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU is designed to monitor progress towards Expert AGI, which is defined as AI systems reaching "at least 90th percentile of skilled adults" in a broad range of tasks. Achieving Expert AGI could lead to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. The benchmark aims to provide a rigorous evaluation framework to track this progress and stimulate development of more capable multimodal models.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating multimodal foundation models on expert-level, college-level multi-discipline tasks; benchmarking large multimodal models (LMMs) on perception, knowledge, and reasoning; monitoring progress towards Expert AGI; stimulating development of next-generation multimodal foundation models.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information, per the ethical considerations in the data annotation protocol.

null_reasons.license: No license is stated in the paper, and the HuggingFace dataset listing shows null for license.
null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not specify a fixed number of independent annotations per item; questions were collected and reviewed but no per-item annotation count is given.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific start/end dates or collection period are mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not discuss missing data handling in the collection process.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described; the dataset consists of discrete Q&A items without missing value imputation.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation (augmentation, resampling, etc.) is described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No explicit versioning or maintenance plan is described beyond the version change log in the paper appendix.
null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: No machine annotation tools were used in the annotation pipeline; questions were manually collected and reviewed by human annotators.
